newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Finance industry sees bad year for Colombia coffee.
newsitem.headline: Finance industry sees bad year for Colombia coffee.

text.p: Falling international prices, a strengthening peso and rising inflation herald another bad year for Colombian coffee, the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) said.
In addition to external factors, ANIF, in its weekly report, said coffee growers have not been given effective official assistance to restructure their debts.
"In the 1996-97 year, coffee will continue facing problems," the association said.

The 1995-96 coffee year, which ended last week, was said by industry insiders to have been the worst since the collapse of the International Coffee Agreement in 1989. ANIF predicted that the National Coffee Fund, which uses the proceeds of coffee sales to purchase the new crop from growers, will post a 120 billion peso deficit for the 1995-96 year once full results are published -- three times higher than forecast.

If the peso's strengthening and inflation continue unchecked, production costs will rise at the same time as export profits fall leading to a deficit of more than 180 billion pesos in 1996- 97, ANIF said.

The National Coffee Fund is managed by the National Coffee Growers' Federation and is seen as a guide to the health of the industry. The International Monetary Fund forecasts a six percent rise in the value of the peso against the dollar, ANIF said in its report, and even worst case predictions put world coffee production for 1996-97 at 100 million sacks -- well above demand levels.
"That situation is due to the recovery of production levels in Brazil which are expected to be between 28 million and 30 million sacks," ANIF said.
